title: Blue Harbor Retail: refund request with revoked consent
transcript:
Agent: Blue Harbor support, this is Noah. How can I help?
Customer: Hi Noah, this is Dana from Blue Harbor Retail. I want a refund for order BH-7734. The replacements keep arriving damaged, and we have wasted enough time.
Agent: I understand. Let me check the account and the order. I see the original order, the first replacement, and the second replacement from July 1. I also see that your account has refund processing turned off.
Customer: Turned off? We opted out of automatic refunds a while ago, but this is a damaged order. Can you make an exception?
Agent: I am not able to issue a refund from this line while the account consent is disabled. I can escalate the request to your account manager, or I can arrange a third replacement with an inspection before it ships.
Customer: We do not want another replacement. We want the money back. Who can approve it?
Agent: Your account manager can review the consent settings and approve an exception. I am creating a high-priority escalation with the order history and the damage photos. I will also ask them to call you today.
Customer: Please do. This has gone on long enough.
Agent: I have created the escalation and assigned it to the account manager. The ticket references order BH-7734 and both damaged replacements. If you do not hear back by the end of the day, call us and ask for the account manager directly.
Customer: Thank you. I appreciate you not just saying no.
Agent: Of course. I am sorry we could not resolve it on this call.
